clue.text: Underworld figure a new painter like Picasso laid bare

parts.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

indicators.note: stripped bare means the outer layer is taken off, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Picasso was a Cubist; dropping the outer letters of that word leaves its core

explanation.surface: An art-world tale of some shadowy figure exposing a modern painter in the Picasso mould.
explanation.walkthrough: CUBIST loses C and T to give UBIS, after A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Anubis is the jackal-headed Egyptian god who guided the dead through the afterlife.

clue.text: Story born yesterday about rook and rodent

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the rest

parts.note: someone who was not born yesterday is worldly, so the phrase means gullible
R is the chess notation for rook
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A tale about a naive youngster, a chess rook and a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born yesterday' is an idiom for gullible; the rook is the chess piece, standing as its notation letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, which is what a story is.

clue.text: Grandiose wine at bottom of tank cold

parts.note: to tank and to bomb both mean to fail badly
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A pompous wine description: something chilly sitting at the bottom of a vat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, one piece 'at bottom of' another comes after it. 'Tank' looks like a container but is a verb, to flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombastic means pompous and inflated in language, a grandiose way of speaking.

clue.text: Collector of rings and fancy coins

indicators.note: fancy as a verb-turned-adjective suggests something elaborated or made over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A hobbyist who amasses jewellery and ornate coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The collector sounds like a jeweller; it is a video-game hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic the Hedgehog, the Sega video-game character, gathers gold rings as he runs.

clue.text: Car company compresses hydrogen — a large fuel source

indicators.note: to compress something is to squeeze it inside, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: car plus CO, the usual abbreviation for company
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A motor firm squeezing hydrogen into its business plan, hoping for a big energy source.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes just after the C of CAR to give CHAR, then CO, A and L follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal is burnt wood used as fuel in barbecues and forges, so it is a source of heat.

clue.text: Most remote bird eating leeks on occasion

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater

parts.note: a coot is a water bird

indicators.note: on occasion means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of leeks

explanation.surface: A bird pecking at leeks from time to time in the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' suggests distance, but here it means emotionally distant.
explanation.definitionFit: Coolest here means most aloof or distant in manner, the least warm and friendly.

clue.text: Put together dope crest spending millions on diamonds

indicators.note: spending money uses it up, so that letter is no longer there

parts.note: a dope and an ass are both fools
a crest is a heraldic emblem
M is the abbreviation for million
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: An idiot blows a fortune on diamonds for his family coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Ms in the crest word is spent; diamonds is the card suit, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembled means fitted or gathered together, the past tense of putting parts together.

clue.text: Column bloke is rewriting

indicators.note: rewriting produces a new version, so the letters come out in another order

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A newspaper column that some man is busy redrafting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' suggests a newspaper piece but means a stone pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone pillar, a kind of monumental column.

clue.text: Bully essentially harassed teen in kind

indicators.note: harassed means agitated and pushed around, so the letters are jumbled
essentially points to a word's essence, its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of bully
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A bully torments a teenager in a similar way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In kind' reads as 'likewise', but 'in' is part of the jumbled letters and kind alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means merciful and tolerant, gentle in judgement, as a kind person is.

clue.text: Doctor mentored us with excellence

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective: possessing excellence

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A doctor who supervised us with great distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person but is a verb telling you to rework the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous in its informal sense means outstanding or superb, the quality of excellence.

clue.text: Plant found by river in bog

indicators.note: one item sits in another, so these letters go inside the following word

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A botanist spots a plant growing beside a river in marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside FEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless green plant with feathery fronds, common in damp places.

clue.text: Very funny situation includes a boy dressing

indicators.note: something that includes another thing holds it inside

parts.note: a scream is informally something hilarious
a plus lad, a boy

explanation.surface: A hilarious scene in which a young lad is getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAD sits after the S of SCREAM. Salad cream is a tangy British condiment, like a thin mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a sauce poured over salads, which is what a dressing is.

clue.text: Very popular electronic video service that was shut down

definitions.text: video service that was shut down

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
in means fashionable or popular
E is the usual prefix abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A one-time hit online video platform that has since closed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a straight description, so the first three words quietly split into abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Vine was a short-looping video app owned by Twitter, discontinued in 2017.

clue.text: Turn away from neighbourhood area for one further on?

indicators.note: X for Y means one letter stands in place of another, and 'further on' picks the later of two candidates

parts.note: a district is a neighbourhood
A is the abbreviation for area
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Moving away from one's neighbourhood to a region further along.
explanation.walkthrough: DISTRICT has two Is; the second, further on, becomes A to give DISTRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract is to divert someone's attention, turning it away from what they were doing.

clue.text: American news spun Republican departing with additional comments

indicators.note: something departing leaves, so that letter goes from the word

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
news read as plural of N, the abbreviation for new
to rotate is to spin
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: US media putting a spin on a Republican's exit, with extra commentary.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking news as two Ns, the plural of the new abbreviation, is a setter's liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Annotated describes a text supplied with notes, explanatory remarks added in the margins.

clue.text: Start to launch missile right away in case

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of launch

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a rocket is a missile
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An order to fire a missile at once, should the need arise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' reads as 'if needed', but case alone is the definition and 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A locket is a small hinged case worn on a necklace, holding a picture or keepsake.

clue.text: Stick around cinema for ending with grandeur

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: to cling is to stick
IMAX is a big-screen cinema format

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay in the cinema for a film's grand finale.
explanation.walkthrough: IMAX is a brand of giant-screen cinema, so it can stand for cinema in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Climaxing means reaching a peak, finishing on a high or dramatic note.

clue.text: You bet after lone card originally turned? Fold!

indicators.note: after places the opening phrase later, so 'You bet' is sent second, below the rest in this down entry
turned means twisted round into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of card
you bet and sure are both enthusiastic yeses

explanation.surface: A poker player with a single card face up decides to fold rather than bet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the piece that comes after sits below. 'Fold' looks like a poker move but means a pen for sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold is a pen for livestock, an enclosure where sheep are kept.

clue.text: Almost run aground close to lighthouse

indicators.note: almost means nearly but not quite, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to beach a boat is to run it aground
on can mean near or adjacent, as in a town on the coast

explanation.surface: A ship nearly runs aground right next to a lighthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Beaching a vessel means running it ashore deliberately or by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal light or fire for guiding ships, which is what a lighthouse provides.

clue.text: A fire boosted by this roars

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hand-pumped device that blows air onto a fire
second meaning: shouts loudly, a verb

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one sentence about a fire roaring; the two parts are separate meanings, a noun and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the blower used to feed air to a hearth; as a verb the word means bawls loudly.

clue.text: A sucker for soldiers?

parts.note: surface reading: someone who cannot resist a man in uniform; setter's reading: soldiers are insects of a colony, and this beast sucks them up with a long tongue

explanation.walkthrough: Soldier is a caste in insect colonies, so the 'sucker' is an animal that feeds on them.
explanation.definitionFit: This African mammal, the aardvark, licks up termites and other insects with its sticky tongue.

clue.text: Ultimately drove Vauxhall right into ditch — weird!

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only final letters are taken

parts.note: the closing letters of drove and Vauxhall

indicators.note: a thing driven into another ends up inside it

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A driver finally steers a Vauxhall car into a ditch, and it's bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes just after the D of DITCH. Vauxhall is a British car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldritch is a literary word meaning eerie or unearthly, strange in a sinister way.

clue.text: Display slice of austere gateau on the counter

indicators.note: counter means contrary, so the letters run against the usual direction
a slice is a portion cut from a whole, so the letters come from inside the phrase

parts.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A shop shows a portion of a plain cake on its counter.
explanation.walkthrough: In the shop picture the counter is furniture; here it signals going backwards up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a set of open shelves used to display ornaments, a display stand.

clue.text: We should punch, knocking out fellow second

indicators.note: knocking someone out removes them from the fight, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a left is a punch thrown with the left hand
F is the abbreviation for fellow
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A boxer's corner urging a punch to floor the opponent's second.
explanation.walkthrough: LEFT without F gives LET, then S. 'Punch' looks like a verb but is a noun, a boxing blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Let's is the contraction of let us, used to propose that we ought to do something.

clue.text: Art lover at renovated airport moves people with this?

indicators.note: something renovated is rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An art enthusiast at a refurbished airport wonders how passengers get moved about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' does double duty in the surface but belongs to the letters to rework; the question mark flags a descriptive definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelator is a moving walkway, the flat conveyor that carries passengers along airport corridors.

clue.text: Mechanic at the rear stops to modify Fiat

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, sitting inside

parts.note: to edit is to modify

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of mechanic

explanation.surface: A mechanic at the back of the garage halts work on a Fiat car.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiat looks like the Italian car brand but is the definition, a Latin word for decree.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative decree or order, which is exactly what an edict is.

clue.text: Candid old writer

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author but is just the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Open describes someone frank and unconcealed, a synonym of candid.

clue.text: We are discovered moving Shiite jug at start of prayer

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so the letters change order

parts.note: letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of prayer

explanation.surface: Worshippers caught out while shifting a Shiite water jug as prayers begin.
explanation.definitionFit: The jig is up is an idiom announcing that a trick or scheme has been exposed.

clue.text: European left darts having bagged 500 doubles in separate legs

indicators.note: to double back is to retrace one's path, so the string is read in the opposite direction
bagging something puts it inside a holder

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A darts match report: a European player bagging a big score with doubles across separate legs.
explanation.walkthrough: D slips inside DARTS after its D; E, L and that string then run backwards. Legs and doubles are darts terms, a leg being one game of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to sit or stand astride, with one leg on each side, legs held apart.

clue.text: Animated bouncer set off to throw out boor at last

indicators.note: throwing something out removes it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to trigger something is to set it off

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of boor

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer is provoked into ejecting a lout.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIGGER without R. Bouncer suggests a doorman, but this one bounces on his tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger is the bouncing tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh, made famous by Disney cartoons.
